chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah from Abi Junub from his father from Umar ibn [Abi] al-Miqdam from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
A man passed by him who was being lashed. He said: 'Where was his cornelian ring? Indeed, if he had been wearing it, he would not have been lashed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of wearing an Aqiq (cornelian) ring in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links the physical affliction of lashing to the spiritual state of the individual, noting that the absence of the cornelian (aqiq) ring—a symbol of prophetic authority and divine protection in Shia tradition—meant the man was not shielded from punishment. This highlights the Shia scholarly view that the Aqiq ring serves not merely as adornment but as a tangible means of *hifz* (protection) and a sign of bearing the Imamate's spiritual weight, thereby averting calamities.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali Majluwayh from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim from Ahmad b. Abi Abdillah from Abi Junub from his father from Umar b. [Abi] al-Miqdam from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said: “
Where is his cornelian ring? If he had been wearing that, he would not have been lashed.”
